title: Norway Spruce: Old Norway Spruces You Can Visit
meta_description: Norway spruce grows wild in mountain forests, not cities. Sofia's tallest was planted in 1885 by the writer Ivan Vazov and now dwarfs his own statue.
intro: Norway spruce belongs to mountain forests, the slopes of the Balkans and Scandinavia, not to city parks, so every spruce on this site got there by somebody's deliberate choice. Sofia's tallest, in Borisova Garden, was planted in 1885 by the writer Ivan Vazov and has since outgrown the marble bust raised to him decades later. Near Rothenburg, two spruces stand over a small waterfall in the Vorbachtal, registered by Bavaria as one natural monument rather than two, their exact age unrecorded. In Reykjavik, a spruce on the island of Elliðaárhólmi was named Iceland's Tree of the Year in 2019, twelve metres tall and barely older than most of the visitors who come to see it, proof that a country with almost no native forest left can still grow something worth naming.
